market_context: The Nasdaq-100 fell 1.22% to 27,943.74 (QQQ −1.20% to $679.89) as chip stocks reversed Thursday’s rotation away from Nvidia; the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 3.43%. October PPI rose 0.3%, but the 6.5% annual pace (fastest since November 2022) did little to support tech.
market_cap_basis: Shares outstanding x 2026-11-13 close. Shares implied from Nasdaq market caps as of the 2026-10-29 close (watchlist market_cap_usd / 2026-10-29 close), so multi-class companies (e.g. GOOGL) reflect all share classes.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. Common Stock
stocks.reason: Investors unwound Thursday’s rotation into Nvidia rivals after founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. AMD had rallied sharply over the prior five sessions on bets that customers might shift AI-chip orders, and Friday’s drop was a sector-wide reversal and profit-taking rather than company-specific news.

stocks.name: Cisco Systems Inc. Common Stock (DE)
stocks.reason: Cisco fell in the first regular session after Thursday’s fiscal first-quarter results. Revenue hit a record $18.5 billion, up 24%, non-GAAP EPS was $1.40, and the company raised fiscal 2027 guidance and its hyperscaler AI-infrastructure target to $9 billion, but non-GAAP gross margin slipped to 65.6% from 68.1% on a heavier mix of lower-margin AI networking hardware and higher memory costs, while product-order growth slowed to 21% from 35%. Citi cut its price target to $120 from $139 (keeping Buy), Barclays to $109 from $123 (Equal Weight), and Wells Fargo to $130 from $150 (Overweight).

stocks.name: Lam Research Corporation Common Stock
stocks.reason: Lam slipped with other wafer-fab equipment names after Applied Materials, a close peer, reported a record quarter after Thursday’s close but guided first-quarter revenue to $11.1 billion plus or minus $500 million, below estimates. That outlook bears on the same chipmaker budgets that pay Lam, and the broader semiconductor selloff added pressure.
